notes: The page opens in the middle of a woman senator's speech (she addresses 'señora presidenta' and calls herself 'argentina y pampeana'), unlabelled, so that speech is not listed as a start. It runs for ten justified paragraphs and ends at 'la bandera argentina.'; only then do the two labels appear, both near the foot, and the Artaza turn continues onto the next page. In the chair's label the closing period after the parenthesis is set bold while the surname inside it is roman — one label, recorded as printed. Note the chair is a woman, 'Sra. Presidenta (Rojkés de Alperovich)', while Artaza opens by addressing 'Señor presidente'; that is what the page prints and I did not tidy it. No stenographer notes, no headings, no footnotes, no footer. TYPOGRAPHY: several stretches are rendered in a noticeably thinner, slightly condensed face than the surrounding text — the tail of the first paragraph from 'Y sin todo eso es imposible imaginar un país.' through 'nombrar–', and the last two lines of the Artaza paragraph — as if a different font were substituted mid-paragraph.
